summary: Benchmarked equivalent labeled literal workflows across one, ten and one hundred patterns on sparse and dense UTF-8 fixtures, with one rg process per trial, complete seven-trial paired cells, scan-cost boundaries and automaton growth evidence.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes the reachable completed Search scope commits through W08-S04 and other pre-existing branch commits; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the internal benchmark measurement seam, benchmark executable command, benchmark-focused tests and benchmark documentation were changed. Search matching behavior and public datasource contracts were not changed; automaton counters are internal diagnostics only.

workflows.candidate: Actual SearchManyLiteralScan with one in-process traversal and Aho-Corasick matcher per invocation.
workflows.baseline: One fresh rg process with --json --no-config --no-ignore --fixed-strings and one -e per registered literal, followed by exact-literal pattern labeling.

limitations: The rg label adapter is equivalent only for this unique-literal cohort because rg JSON submatches do not carry the requested pattern identifier.
Native rg traversal/read/matching time is not observable through the subprocess boundary; searched bytes are retained and no native scan duration is invented.
Filesystem cache was unknown and no superiority or threshold claim is promoted.

newScenarios: Equivalent labeled outputs for one, ten and one hundred patterns on sparse and dense fixtures
One rg process invocation per multi-pattern baseline workload
Monotonic Aho-Corasick node, transition and output-reference growth

commands.executionWrapper: Direct PowerShell invocation with separate stdout/stderr capture and retained process handle.

commands.argv: git diff --check; source manifest and artifact hash validation

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release suite exited 0 across 21 projects with 1,482 total tests, 1,448 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the Search focused suite and all new benchmark tests also passed.

The separate ownership review approved the equivalent labeled result unit, process boundary, cache labeling, automaton measurement seam and explicit limitations; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
The independent fixture oracle, managed SearchManyLiteralScan output and one-process rg output agree in all six labeled-occurrence cells across sparse/dense and 1/10/100 pattern workloads.
The benchmark command and documented workflow are executable and describe only the tested unique-literal equivalent baseline; no unsupported public SQL or host contract was added.

The benchmark uses disposable fixture scopes, completes each reader-backed scan before reporting success, retains allocation and traversal counters, and documents unknown cache/process boundaries without introducing shared mutable state.

knownLimitations: This is a scanner/workflow observation, not a datasource, compiled-query, service or client latency qualification.
Duplicate literal labels, regex semantics, filesystem-cold measurements and native rg scan duration remain outside this scope.
The benchmark does not promote a performance threshold or universal implementation choice.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed.

cohorts.Description: Four hit lines across four files; every selected literal is present on each hit line.
Every physical line contains every selected literal.

baseline.invocation: One fresh rg process per trial with --json --no-config --no-ignore --fixed-strings and one -e argument per registered literal.
baseline.labeling: The JSON postprocessor maps each returned submatch's exact literal text to its unique requested pattern identifier. The benchmark deliberately uses unique literals; duplicate literal labels are not claimed equivalent by this external baseline.

candidate.invocation: One in-process SearchManyLiteralScan invocation per trial, including scope traversal, binary probe, decode, Aho-Corasick matching and normalized labeled output.

timingBoundary.scanCost: Candidate scan milliseconds surround the complete in-process eligible traversal/read/decode/match operation before normalized result materialization. For rg, native traversal/read/matching time is not observable through the subprocess boundary; scanned input bytes are retained instead.
timingBoundary.endToEndInvestigationCost: Both candidate and rg timings surround the complete invocation through normalized labeled result sorting, serialization and SHA-256 hashing. The rg value includes process bridge, JSON parsing and literal-to-pattern labeling.

benchmark.cachePolicy: Filesystem cache was not flushed or independently verified on this unprivileged Windows host; cells are labeled unknown and process freshness is recorded separately.
